section_summaries.individual_presentation: difficulty in walking, progressive weakness of the lower extremities, left facial weakness, and an unsteady gait unable to stand without assistance; mild facial asymmetry; severe weakness of the lower extremities; deep tendon reflexes absent; vibration perception impaired at toes and ankles; position sense absent at toes and reduced at finger, joints, wrists, and ankles; developed bifacial paresis malignant blood disease with paraproteinemia and demyelinating neuropathy
section_summaries.individual_diagnostics: Three months earlier, she was diagnosed as having CMML Serum protein immunoelectrophoresis revealed increased IgG protein and two monoclonal bands IgGK and IgGX; IgC did not react with CM1 or CD1a gangliosides; cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed seven cells and protein of 142 mg/dL; nerve conduction studies showed absent sensory response in right median and peroneal nerves and both facial nerves; all distal latencies prolonged; needle EMG showed reduced interference pattern in orbicularis oris bilaterally Sural nerve biopsy interpreted as segmental demyelination without inflammatory infiltrates but with reduction of large myelinated fibers; teased fiber preparations and immunofluorescent studies revealed positive IgG binding; immunohistochemistry revealed positive staining to IgG; absence of inflammatory cells in nerve biopsy
section_summaries.individual_treatment: responded dramatically to high doses of corticosteroids started therapy with 80 mg prednisolone IM treated with 150 mg of intravenous diazepam in 2 days, and 60 mg of oral baclofen daily with minimal effect; one gram of methocarbamol administered intravenously over 1 hour resulted in immediate resolution of spasms; maintained on oral baclofen, diazepam, and methocarbamol
section_summaries.individual_outcome: immediate resolution of spasms with significant improvement of muscle rigidity lasting a few hours; mild headache and lethargy following methocarbamol infusion
section_summaries.individual_limitations: absence of inflammatory cells obliges to call the condition a “GB-like” syndrome with paraproteinemia; the accurate mechanism for pathogenesis of polyneuropathy in patients with paraproteinemia has not been established; this may be due to treatment with corticosteroids No further diagnostic details or treatment and outcome information provided The etiology of this disorder is unknown
